facts.raw_span: A 69-year-old Japanese man presented with pain and a 10-mm polypoid mass on the left lower gingiva
He had undergone chemoradiotherapy 15 years earlier for squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa, with no recurrence until now
He denied tobacco or alcohol use
trismus was present
a rough-surfaced polypoid lesion in the left lower molar gingiva covered by a whitish pseudomembrane
Panoramic radiography showed a moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption
Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated an enhancing soft-tissue mass with irregular mandibular bone destruction
A biopsy specimen showed loose granulation tissue with scattered atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells in a fibrin-rich edematous stroma alongside inflammatory cells
The spindle cells had basophilic cytoplasm, bizarre nuclei, and atypical mitoses; many contained neutrophils within cytoplasmic vacuoles
Immunohistochemical staining revealed that the spindle cells were positive for vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin, p63, p53, and CD68, but negative for pan-cytokeratin and other epithelial markers
Ki-67 labeling index was approximately 50%
These findings prompted consideration of a malignant spindle cell process

concepts.why: The patient has a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa and the current findings suggest a malignant spindle cell process.
The biopsy specimen shows loose granulation tissue with scattered atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells, which is consistent with malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
The spindle cells are positive for vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin, and p63, which suggests a smooth muscle origin, consistent with leiomyosarcoma.
The presence of a whitish pseudomembrane and loose granulation tissue with inflammatory cells suggests an inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor.
The panoramic radiography shows a moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption, which could be consistent with a traumatic bone cyst.
The patient has a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa and the current findings suggest a malignant process in the gingiva.
The biopsy specimen shows atypical spindle cells with basophilic cytoplasm and bizarre nuclei, consistent with spindle cell carcinoma.
The panoramic radiography and CT scans show irregular mandibular bone destruction, which could be consistent with osteosarcoma.
The high Ki-67 labeling index of approximately 50% explains the aggressive nature of the tumor.

rationales.F01: The presence of a polypoid mass on the left lower gingiva is concerning for a malignant process, but the location and appearance are not specific enough to rule in or out any particular diagnosis.
rationales.F02: A history of squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa increases the likelihood of a recurrence or a new primary malignancy in the head and neck region.
rationales.F04: The presence of trismus suggests involvement of the mandible or surrounding tissues, which could be seen in several malignant processes.
rationales.F06: The moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption is highly suggestive of a malignant process, particularly one that involves the bone.
rationales.F08: The presence of atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells in a fibrin-rich edematous stroma alongside inflammatory cells is concerning for a malignant spindle cell process.
rationales.F09: The presence of basophilic cytoplasm, bizarre nuclei, and atypical mitoses in the spindle cells, as well as the presence of neutrophils within cytoplasmic vacuoles, is highly suggestive of a malignant process.
rationales.F10: The immunohistochemical staining pattern, including positivity for vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin, p63, p53, and CD68, and negativity for pan-cytokeratin and other epithelial markers, is consistent with a malignant spindle cell process.
rationales.F11: A high Ki-67 labeling index is concerning for a malignant process with a high proliferative rate.
rationales.F12: The overall clinical and histopathological findings are highly suggestive of a malignant spindle cell process, which could include several different diagnoses.
